title: Asgard fragment (tree/json)
description: A fragment a server returns for a region: one node, or an array of nodes. See protocol.md §9 and §10.
$comment: Rules from §9, §10 and §12.4 that this schema cannot check: (1) A fragment may use only the core types of §9.7 plus the types the client listed in `elements` at the handshake (§6.1, §9.3). That depends on the session, so this schema does not list types at all; it only checks a type's shape. (2) A client refuses a fragment nested deeper than 64 levels (§9.1). JSON Schema has no way to count depth, so that is not checked here. (3) Unknown members of a node, and unknown props, are ignored (§5.3), so this schema allows them. Callback slots and navigations refuse unknown members, and so does this schema. (4) Props of a known type with the wrong value type are treated as absent by the client (§9.7); this schema only checks media URLs. (5) `navigate` must match a route the client knows when tapped (§12.4). (6) `navigate` and media URLs are limited to 2048 bytes; maxLength counts characters, so a value with multi-byte characters can pass here and still be too long. (7) A client may accept `http:` media URLs in a development build (§9.6); this schema allows https only. (8) Keys must be unique among siblings, compared as strings (§9.1).

oneOf.description: Several root nodes, side by side in the region (§9.1).

node.description: One element in the tree (§9.1). It carries no node ids or callback ids; the client makes those (§9.2). Members this schema does not name are ignored (§5.3).

type.description: The element type name: a core type (§9.7) or one the client advertised. The client decides whether it can render it (§9.4).

key.description: Stable identity among siblings, compared as a string. Relative to the parent, never an id (§9.2).

class.description: Space-separated style utility names, resolved by the client (§9.7).

allOf.description: §9.7: a text node's children are text runs.
§9.3: a web view in a fragment must not load the client's own local content.

local.description: Must be off. A local web view loads the client's own content.

props.description: Presentational props, written by the server (§9.3, §9.7). Props a type does not define are ignored.

propertyNames.description: §9.3: names beginning _, native- or native: are reserved.

leadingAvatar.description: Used by the well-known list_item type when a client advertises it (§9.7).

leadingImage.description: Used by the well-known list_item type when a client advertises it (§9.7).

mediaUrl.description: A URL the client loads: an absolute https URL with a host. null or an empty string mean no image, as does leaving the prop out (§9.6).

pressSlot.description: A press slot: a method call, a navigation or a back (§10.1, §12.4).

valueSlot.description: A change or submit slot. It can only call a method; the control's value is appended to args (§10.1). It cannot navigate (§12.4).

call.description: Runs a method. On the server by default, or in the client with target client (§10.2, §10.3). Unknown members are refused (§5.3).

args.description: Arguments, passed in order. A server always sends this, even when empty; a client treats a missing one as empty.

target.description: Where the method runs. Absent means server.

navigate.description: Moves the app to an app path (§12.4). Unknown members are refused (§5.3).
An app path: one leading slash, no scheme or host, no backslash, no whitespace or control characters.

replace.description: Replace the current screen instead of pushing a new one.

back.description: Goes back one screen (§12.4). Unknown members are refused (§5.3).

transition.description: One of the client's screen transitions.

argValue4.description: An argument: a plain JSON value, nested at most 4 deep.

argValue3.description: A plain JSON value, nested at most 3 more deep.

argValue2.description: A plain JSON value, nested at most 2 more deep.

argValue1.description: A plain JSON value, nested at most 1 more deep.

argScalar.description: null, a boolean, a number or a string.
